Definition: powerful (specifically, a paw); by implication, numerous
BiblicalUsage: Mighty and numerous is the word for nations too strong to count, and it follows Israel into the land. Seven nations greater and mightier than Israel stood before them, the cities were great and fenced up to heaven, Amos says the mighty oppress the just and take a bribe, and Daniel says the king of fierce countenance will destroy wonderfully and will prosper and practise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe might is measured by God, not by numbers, because the nations greater than Israel fell before a people with no army of their own. The mighty who oppress the just will answer for it, and I hold that the power that looks unbreakable is the one God breaks first.
